propositions: User identity is resolved differently in Cloud (opaque accountId) and Data Center (name), and this difference must be pinned in a stable UserIdentityModel protocol to prevent leaks into mapper and transport logic.
PR #120's implementation with getattr-discovered _assignee_resolver was unreachable for DC, causing authoritative=False always and triggering assignee-diff churn on every pass rather than converging.
NameIdentity must perform real lookup against DC user-search endpoint to return authoritative=True for resolvable assignees, eliminating the churn class defect.

AccountIdIdentity (Cloud) and NameIdentity (DC) implementations must both satisfy an identical 3-state resolution contract via parameterized unit tests covering converged, diverged, and unresolvable states.
An unresolvable assignee must raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError for both models rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value.
Cloud's existing J1-pinned assignee behavior must remain unchanged when AccountIdIdentity is injected at Cloud backend construction.
